topic: ChatGPT vs Google: How LLMs Work
description: Test your understanding of retrieval vs generation, hallucinations, base models, and how tools extend LLM capabilities.

questions.question: What is the core difference between Google Search and ChatGPT?
options: Google is free, ChatGPT is paid
Google retrieves from an index; ChatGPT generates from learned patterns
Google uses AI, ChatGPT does not
questions.explanation: Google searches its pre-built index of web pages and returns ranked links (retrieval). ChatGPT predicts and generates answers from training patterns (generation). This is the fundamental difference.

questions.question: How does an LLM generate its response to your prompt?
options: It searches the live internet in real time
It predicts the next word/token based on probability from training data
It looks up answers in a pre-written FAQ database
questions.explanation: LLMs work like smart autocomplete — they predict the most likely next token based on patterns learned during training. 'The sun rises in...' → 'the east' because that's the highest probability.

questions.question: What is a 'base model' in the context of LLMs?
options: The final chatbot product users interact with
The raw core AI that only predicts next text — before instruction tuning and tools
A model trained only on books, not internet data
questions.explanation: Base model = engine (predicts next token). ChatGPT/Claude/Gemini = car with features added on top (instruction tuning, safety, tools, web search). Companies never expose raw base models directly.

questions.question: What is an AI hallucination?
options: When the AI refuses to answer a question
When the AI makes up information and presents it confidently as fact
When the AI gives a correct but short answer
questions.explanation: Hallucination happens when AI generates plausible-sounding but false information. It's not lying — it's guessing the next best word. Fluent language ≠ factual accuracy. 'Tez bolne se koi baat sahi nahi ho jati.'

questions.question: What is the difference between training and inference?
options: Training is for Google; inference is for ChatGPT
Training is the learning phase; inference is when the model answers your questions
They are the same process with different names
questions.explanation: Training = school phase where AI studies massive data (expensive, done once). Inference = working phase where the trained model generates answers to your prompts in real time.

questions.question: What is RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation)?
options: A type of neural network layer
Combining external evidence retrieval with LLM text generation
A method to train LLMs faster
questions.explanation: RAG = web search + LLM. Retrieval provides external evidence (facts from documents/web), and generation gives you a natural-language answer. Key concept for real-world AI applications.

questions.question: Why do LLMs have a 'knowledge cutoff' date?
options: Models are deleted after that date
Retraining on new data is complex and expensive — models aren't updated daily
The internet stops producing new content after that date
questions.explanation: Training is price-heavy and time-consuming. Models are trained on data available up to a certain date. Current info often comes from tools like web search, not from retraining.
